page.account.logoutHint: Ends your session with the login system (auth.war) - you'll need to log in again to come back to nspawnmgr.

field.name: Name
page.create.title: New Nspawn
page.create.rdpUnavailableHint: RDP isn't available for this template — see its own "RDP" setting on the Templates admin page for why.
page.newPod.commandHint: The command run as the pod's main process, like a Dockerfile CMD - left blank, the pod trusts whatever command the template's own image already has built in. If that's a plain interactive shell (or anything else that doesn't keep running on its own), the pod will exit within moments of starting - it won't fail to create, but it'll immediately show as stopped again. Editable later from the pod's own page, but only takes effect the next time it's recreated (the pod must be stopped first).
page.newPod.accessHint: SSH, RDP, and VNC access aren't set up automatically for a pod - enable them from the pod's own page once it's running.
page.newQemu.title: New QEMU VM
page.newQemu.noTemplatesHint: (none yet - use "Create template from this machine" on a stopped VM's own page to make one)
page.newQemu.nicModelHint: Some older guest OSes need a specific model to see any network at all - e.g. FreeDOS typically needs "pcnet".
page.newQemu.pointerDeviceHint: USB tablet fixes mouse-cursor drift in VNC for GUI guests, but DOS-family OSes have no USB support and need PS/2.
page.newQemu.noIsosHint: No ISOs uploaded yet — see the Packages admin page. The VM can still be created with an empty disk and no boot media, but nothing useful will happen until an ISO is mounted from its own page.
page.newQemu.bootHint: The VM boots straight from its ISO (installer) until an OS is actually installed onto the disk and the ISO is ejected from the VM's own page — the same "boot device" switch stays available afterward, e.g. to run a repair disc later.
page.newQemu.accessHint: VNC console access is configured automatically (a Connect button appears once the VM is running). SSH and RDP aren't set up automatically — enable them from the VM's own page once a guest OS with those services is installed and running.
page.detail.externalHostHint: Admin-configured external host — nspawnmgr does not control its lifecycle.
page.detail.createTemplateHint: Packs this machine's current rootfs into a brand-new, independent template (visible on /admin/templates afterwards) - only while this machine is STOPPED, since packing a live rootfs risks an inconsistent archive as files change mid-tar.
page.detail.portMappingsHint: Changes here require a restart to take effect.
page.detail.outboundAllowLabel: Allow this container to reach the internet
page.detail.outboundAllowlistHint: Specific destinations to still allow when the above is off, without granting full internet access. Other managed containers are already reachable by name (see the administrator guide) as long as *this* container's own outbound access isn't disabled - this is for one specific external destination when it is:
page.detail.containerUsersHint: Listed live while the container is running; shows the last-known list otherwise. Adding a user or changing a password needs the container running — if it isn't (or no stored sudo secret is configured), the request waits for an admin to approve it.
page.detail.primaryAccountHint: SSH/RDP/VNC currently connect as {0}. Use "Make primary" below to switch to any other account in this list — same approval rules as adding a user or changing a password.
page.detail.sshCredentialsHint: nspawnmgr has no stored SSH credential for this machine. If it's stuck in BOOTING, this is usually why — without one, nspawnmgr can't confirm SSH is reachable and it never flips to RUNNING. If this machine already has SSH access set up some other way, record its account name and private key here so nspawnmgr can use them.
page.detail.remoteAccessHint: For a protocol nspawnmgr didn't set up itself (a discovered machine, or RDP declined when this container was created) — checks the port is actually listening before connecting it to Guacamole. You'll be prompted for credentials each time you connect, since nspawnmgr doesn't generate or store an account for it.
page.detail.rdpSecurityHint: Guacamole's RDP negotiation mode. Leave on ANY unless RDP fails to connect — some xrdp versions (e.g. Fedora's) reject ANY for reasons unrelated to credentials; RDP (classic security) is the known workaround. Applies immediately if RDP is already connected, no restart needed.
page.detail.pamHint: Replaces this container's own local password check for whichever services are ticked below, checking the source selected instead — useful when a container's local login is broken, or to reuse nspawnmgr's own login backend. Applies immediately if the container is running; otherwise takes effect the next time it starts. Choosing "nspawnmgr auth backend" lets any user who can authenticate against that backend log in as this container's account — this container's own owner/sharing list isn't consulted by this check.
page.detail.packageManagerHint: This machine has no template, so nspawnmgr doesn't otherwise know which package manager it uses. Set it here to enable package installation below.
page.detail.installPackageHint: Packages an admin has uploaded for this container's package manager (see the Packages admin page). For APT, a missing dependency is detected and fetched automatically before installing (it shows up in the Packages admin page afterward, same as any other auto-fetched package). Other package managers install the file directly — a missing dependency there shows up as a visible error below, it's not fixed automatically.
page.detail.noPackagesUploaded: No packages uploaded for this container's package manager yet.
page.detail.removableMediaHint: Mounted read-only at a fixed /mnt/cdrom, like a real CD drive — at most one ISO at a time. A persistent setting, same as port mappings: changes here take effect the next time the container is (re)started, and stay configured across restarts until explicitly changed or ejected.
page.detail.noIsosUploadedShort: No ISOs uploaded yet — see the Packages admin page.
page.detail.machineSettingsHint: Read live from the host itself, not stored in nspawnmgr's own database — an admin may change these directly on the host (e.g. via systemctl), so nspawnmgr always shows the host's own current state rather than risking a stale cached value.
page.detail.bootSettingsUnavailable: Could not determine this machine's boot settings right now — try reloading the page.
page.detail.autoStartLabel: Start automatically when the host boots
page.detail.scriptsHint: Named, reusable scripts run inside this container as root. Anyone this container is shared with can create, edit, delete, and run them, same as the owner.
page.detail.mustBeRunningToConnect: Container must be running to connect.
page.detail.noAccessConfigured: No managed SSH/RDP/VNC access configured yet — see Remote access above.
page.files.title: Files
page.files.sftpHint: This container has no host-visible filesystem - browsing it goes over SFTP against its own SSH server instead. Enter a credential that can log in over SSH; it's held only for this browser session and is never saved.
page.files.sftpBrowseHint: Browses over SFTP as the connected account - not capped at its home directory, bounded only by that account's own permissions, same as any real SFTP client. Click a folder to open it, double-click a file to download it, or drag and drop a file onto the list below to upload it into the current folder (up to 200MB).
page.files.directBrowseHint: Browses this container's filesystem directly - works whether or not the container is running. Click a folder to open it, double-click a file to download it, or drag and drop a file onto the list below to upload it into the current folder (up to 200MB).
page.podDetail.subtitle: Pod (podman)
page.podDetail.commandHint: The command run as this pod's main process, like a Dockerfile CMD - left blank, the pod trusts whatever command its image already has built in. If that's a plain interactive shell (or anything else that doesn't keep running on its own), the pod will exit within moments of starting - or, if the image has no command at all, it'll fail to start entirely. Changing this only takes effect the next time the pod is recreated, which happens automatically on Save - only available while the pod is stopped, or in ERROR (e.g. it never managed to start at all - this is how you'd fix that).
page.podDetail.remoteAccessHint: Checks the port is actually listening before connecting it to Guacamole. You'll be prompted for credentials each time you connect, since nspawnmgr doesn't generate or store an account for a pod.
page.podDetail.packageManagerHint: This pod has no template, so nspawnmgr doesn't otherwise know which package manager it uses. Set it here to enable package installation below.
page.podDetail.installPackageHint: Packages an admin has uploaded for this pod's package manager (see the Packages admin page).
page.podDetail.noPackagesUploaded: No packages uploaded for this pod's package manager yet.
page.podDetail.scriptsHint: Named, reusable scripts run inside this pod (via podman exec) as root. Anyone this pod is shared with can create, edit, delete, and run them, same as the owner.
page.podDetail.mustBeRunningToConnect: Pod must be running to connect.
page.qemuDetail.subtitle: QEMU VM
page.qemuDetail.stopHint: "Stop" asks the guest OS to shut down (an ACPI request) — it does nothing until an OS is actually installed. "Force stop" always works, no guest cooperation needed.
page.qemuDetail.createTemplateHint: Copies this VM's current disk into a brand-new, independent template (visible on /admin/templates afterwards, and selectable from the New QEMU page's "From template" option) - only while this VM is STOPPED, since copying a live disk risks an inconsistent image as the guest writes to it.
page.qemuDetail.remoteAccessHint: VNC connects to this VM's own hypervisor console — the same screen a physical monitor would show, working even before a guest OS is installed. It's configured automatically; there's nothing to enable. SSH and RDP connect to services running inside the guest OS instead — enable them once one is installed and running, same reachability check as any other container.
page.qemuDetail.removableMediaHint: The VM's boot CD-ROM device. Swapping it here takes effect immediately if the VM is currently running (no restart needed) and also becomes the default for its next boot — the same "boot device" a physical machine's optical drive would be.
page.qemuDetail.mustBeRunningToConnect: VM must be running to connect.

page.adminUsers.subtitle: Manage user roles
page.adminUsers.notDiscoveredHint: nspawnmgr's own self-hosted container hasn't been discovered yet — see the Machines page.
page.adminUsers.externallyManagedNotice: Role is externally managed for this deployment (nspawnmgr.auth.user-is-admin-json is configured) — roles are derived from the identity backend on every login and cannot be changed here.
page.adminSettings.subtitle: Global application configuration
hint.hostExternalHostname: The hostname/DNS name users outside this host should use — what goes in a browser's address bar, and what the "Refresh" buttons below fill into every Guacamole/Auth URL (alongside the protocol/port they already pull from Tomcat). Seeded to this machine's actual hostname on .deb installs; defaults to localhost otherwise.
hint.hostPublicAddress: Not the same as External hostname above — this is what Guacamole's guacd uses to reach a custom port mapping's host-forwarded port (ordinary SSH/RDP/VNC always dial a container's own internal address directly, bypassing this). 10.100.0.1 (nspawnbr0's own address) on a packaged install, since guacd runs inside nspawnmgr's own self-hosted machine and those forwards are bound on the bare host's network stack, not any particular container's.
hint.authWarDetected: auth.war was detected at the configured login URL. These settings are mirrored to a shared file auth.war reads on every request — changes take effect immediately, no restart needed.
field.authRequiredGroup: Required Unix group (pam backend only, optional)
field.authSmbRequiredShare: Required SMB share (smb backend only, optional)
hint.sshTested: Changing these is tested with a real SSH connection before being accepted — see docs/administrator-guide.md §3 "The sudo-capable SSH account".
field.sshPrivateKeyPath: Private key path (used instead of password if set)
hint.nspawnPrivilegedScriptsDir: Must match /etc/sudoers.d/nspawnmgr_exec's hardcoded paths, or every privileged operation (container start/stop, outbound access, Restart Tomcat below) will start failing — sudo fails safe by simply refusing the new path, it does not follow this setting.
hint.dnsUpstreamServers: Comma-separated IP addresses (e.g. a corporate DNS server) that managed containers' non-.internal lookups (apt/dnf/pacman mirrors, etc.) are forwarded to. Defaults to 1.1.1.1,9.9.9.9.
hint.qemuVncPortRange: TCP ports on nspawnbr0's own address (10.100.0.1) that QEMU VMs' VNC listeners are allocated from, one per VM. Must both be set (or both left blank to use the default) and be 5900 or higher. Defaults to 5900-5999.
hint.guacamoleDataSource: Must match whatever your guacamole-auth-jdbc extension calls itself in guacamole.properties (see the Guacamole section below) — shown in red if it doesn't currently match. "Refresh" copies the detected value across.
hint.guacamolePropertiesIntro: Saving does not restart Tomcat. Guacamole will not see these changes until you run sudo systemctl restart tomcat9. Existing values are pulled from the file on this page load and shown below, including any already-configured password (shown masked, as usual for a password field) — field labels and descriptions are sourced from the Apache Guacamole manual.
field.guacamoleSchemaScriptsDirectory: Schema scripts directory (for Test, below — not saved)
hint.guacamoleSchemaScripts: Only needed if Test reports the schema isn't set up yet — point this at the schema/ folder from the guacamole-auth-jdbc extension (matching your database type above), and Test will offer to run every .sql file there, in order. Unlike guacd/guacamole-tomcat below, guacamole-auth-jdbc isn't an apt package on any Debian/Ubuntu release — it's always a downloaded tarball. Prefilled above with nspawnmgr's own opinionated install location, /etc/guacamole/guacamole-auth-jdbc/ — this is where install-guacamole-auth-jdbc.sh puts it (run automatically by the .deb's postinst, or runnable by hand — see docs/administrator-guide.md §7); edit the field if you extracted it somewhere else.
hint.tomcatRestart: Takes effect only after a restart — use the Restart Tomcat button below. If you change the port or enable/disable HTTPS, use the "Refresh hostname/port/protocol" buttons above (Guacamole base URL, auth URLs) to update them to match — they pull the protocol/port from here and the hostname from External hostname above. See docs/administrator-guide.md §6.
hint.tomcatCertificateKeyFile: The tomcat system user needs read access to both files — see §6 "Enabling HTTPS" if you're using Let's Encrypt/Certbot.

page.diagnostics.title: nspawnmgr — Admin: Diagnostics
page.diagnostics.subtitle: Check host prerequisites for container networking
page.diagnostics.hint: Checks the host prerequisites most likely to silently break container networking (SSH/RDP never becoming reachable, containers stuck in BOOTING), plus whether optional container/VM backends (podman, QEMU) are installed. Runs automatically every time this page is opened. Some checks have a "Fix" button — applying a fix asks for your sudo password fresh each time.
page.diagnostics.confirmFix: This changes host configuration (network/firewall/installed packages). Continue?
page.adminPackages.title: nspawnmgr — Admin: Packages
page.adminPackages.subtitle: Upload and manage installable packages and ISO images
page.adminPackages.hint: Packages uploaded here can be installed by any owner onto a container using the matching package manager (see each container's own "Install package" section). No automatic dependency resolution — a missing dependency shows up as a visible error when installed, it's not fixed automatically. Choosing ISO as the package manager uploads a mountable ISO image instead — those show up under a container's "Removable media" section, to be mounted (not installed), one at a time, like a real CD drive.
page.adminPackages.noPackages: No packages uploaded yet — use the + button above to add one.
page.adminPackages.transitiveDependencie: Installing a package with unresolved dependencies (APT/DNF/PACMAN) pre-fetches those dependencies onto the host too, but they're deliberately never listed in the table above individually - a single desktop-environment install can pull in ~450 of them, which would be noise, not a usable table. This generates a list on demand straight from the host's own cache directory instead; nothing here is stored in the database.

page.packageForm.downloadHint: Downloaded directly by the host in the background - large files (e.g. an install ISO) don't need to pass through your own browser upload at all.

page.templateDetail.confirmDeleteTemplat: Delete this template? This cannot be undone.
page.templateForm.sourcePathLabel: Source name (bare name, no extension - resolves to TEMPLATES_DIR/<backend>/<name>.tar.gz; pick a suggestion below or type your own)
page.templateForm.packageManagerLabel: Package manager (none = no way to install SSH/RDP/VNC/desktop packages via this template - the options below that need one are disabled)
page.templateForm.sshPreFetchLabel: SSH pre-fetch packages override (comma-separated package names; blank = package-manager default. Lets a distro package rename be fixed here instead of a code change - e.g. Fedora's tigervnc-server → tigervnc-x11-server.)
page.templateForm.sshStateHint: Preinstalled: the template's own image already has openssh installed and enabled - skips the redundant install/enable step when a container is created from it. Not capable: there's no way to install it via this template (e.g. no package manager).
page.templateForm.vncXstartupHint: A shell command with a single %s for the desktop session command (e.g. startxfce4), used to write the .vnc/xstartup script. Default is a bare exec, TigerVNC's own natural behavior - logging out ends the VNC session (TigerVNC 1.12+ kills Xvnc the instant the xstartup script's own process exits); the next connection attempt starts a fresh one automatically.
page.templateForm.vncProcessNamePatternH: Matches the VNC server binary's own process name, anchored as "(^|/)<pattern> :0 " against a process's full command line (tolerating the absolute path it's normally invoked with) - used to find and kill a stale instance before starting a fresh one. Default X[a-z]*vnc matches both Xvnc and Xtigervnc (the actual binary name Debian's tigervnc-standalone-server execs).
page.templateForm.privateUsersModeLabel: PrivateUsers mode (blank = follow the host's own systemd-nspawn default; IDENTITY keeps a real per-container user namespace but without shifting container UID 0 away from host UID 0 - needed on Fedora for PAM helpers like unix_chkpwd to read /etc/shadow correctly)
